title: Amplification of a probability guarantee
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, let $t\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0\le\varepsilon$, and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every input $x$, $N$ halts on every branch within $t(|x|)$ steps and outputs the membership indicator for $L$ with probability at least $1/2+\varepsilon$. The machine formed by the specified amplification construction with parameter $2n$, using the threshold that accepts at least $n+1$ positive votes among its $2n+1$ executions, halts on every branch within $t(|x|)+2n(2t(|x|)+3)+1$ steps and outputs the membership indicator for $L$ with probability at least $1-2(1-4\varepsilon^2)^n$ on every input $x$.
